briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Steadies Under the Tax, Rescheduling Hits a Speed Bump, Psychedelics Push Ahead
briefs.top: Michigan operators are finding footing — new stores are opening, flower prices and demand have stabilized under the 24% wholesale tax, and a major-party nominee for governor is campaigning on killing it. Nationally, a procedural DEA pause on rescheduling leaves the medical Schedule III order intact while Curaleaf's Aurora bid, Compass Pathways' new U.S. office, and fresh state sales records show the industry's growth story is still very much alive.

local.text: Bloom City Club opens Ypsilanti doors — Ann Arbor-based Bloom City Club launched a new Ypsilanti dispensary and is running cannabis-themed events all month to mark the expansion.
Bay City turns weed tax into beds — Commissioners are set to approve $150,000 in local cannabis tax revenue to keep an overnight homeless drop-in center open for another year.

Flower prices hold, demand stays steady — Despite the new 24% wholesale tax, Michigan flower prices have stayed near all-time lows through early 2026 while consumer demand held firm, leaving retailers with the upper hand.
GOP nominee vows to kill wholesale tax — Governor candidate John James has pledged to repeal or sharply cut the 24% wholesale tax, courting the state's cannabis industry ahead of November's election.

State cracks down on bad actors — Regulators revoked 20 cultivation licenses and hit one grower with a $2 million fine for shipping dirt labeled as marijuana, while Muha Meds lost its Ypsilanti dispensary license.

national.text: DEA hits pause, not reverse — A chief administrative law judge stayed broader marijuana rescheduling hearings over a new GAO report, but the pause leaves April's Schedule III order for medical marijuana and FDA-approved products untouched, with responses due October 13.
Curaleaf raises Aurora takeover bid — Curaleaf sweetened its hostile offer for Aurora Cannabis to $5 per share, built from public data, arguing shareholders deserve a fair sale process.
Compass Pathways opens first U.S. office — The psilocybin drugmaker cut the ribbon on a new Jersey City office as its COMP360 depression treatment carries FDA Breakthrough Therapy status.

New York crosses $4 billion in sales — State regulators announced New York dispensaries have now sold more than $4 billion in recreational marijuana since launch, including nearly $1.5 billion so far this year.

Sales grew in 13 of 15 states — Headset data show marijuana sales rose year-over-year in September across the large majority of tracked adult-use markets, a sign of resilient consumer demand nationally.
